domain: A hospitable review of the 'commons' revival in economics — Elinor Ostrom's institutional analysis of shared resources, and the fatal question of what happens when a commons must scale beyond a face-to-face community
topic: A hospitable review of the 'commons' revival in economics — Elinor Ostrom's institutional analysis of shared resources, and the fatal question of what happens when a commons must scale beyond a face-to-face community

movement.gist: Establish genuine admiration for Ostrom's dismantling of the 'tragedy of the commons' orthodoxy — her field-based demonstration that communities have long governed shared resources (irrigation systems, fisheries, forests) without either privatization or state control, work rigorous enough to earn a Nobel in a discipline hostile to her methods.

Survey the actual content: the eight design principles (clear boundaries, congruence between rules and local conditions, collective-choice arrangements, monitoring by the users themselves, graduated sanctions, conflict resolution mechanisms, recognized rights to organize, nested enterprises for larger systems) — presented as a modest, inductive typology drawn from hundreds of case studies, not a theory of everything.

Land the objection: the eighth principle, 'nested enterprises,' is the one doing all the work when the argument is extended to planetary-scale commons like carbon, and it is precisely the principle least supported by her own evidence base, which was drawn almost entirely from small, monitorable, face-to-face communities — the scaling move smuggles in a claim her method never actually tested.

Reframe: the admiration was correct but aimed at the wrong achievement — Ostrom's real contribution was proving the local case could be made empirically at all, not that it composes upward; the thesis emerges as counter-punch: her work is best defended precisely by refusing the scaling ambition others have grafted onto it.

primary.axis: local self-governance vs. the demands of scale
poles: design principles that work because everyone can watch everyone else
problems (climate, oceans, the atmosphere) that have no faces to watch
Ostrom as careful cataloguer of what has worked
Ostrom as reluctant author of a universal formula others demanded from her

tension_system.interaction: the scale problem is what exposes the gap between what Ostrom actually claimed and what her admirers needed her to have claimed, so the secondary tension supplies the mechanism by which the primary one becomes fatal rather than merely difficult
